class_guess: Chaotic Bell (bouncer type): glider between two 8-cell fields, x9/4 cycles, chaotic junk edge on the left
summary: Glider bounces between two 8-cell fields; field grows x9/4 per cycle; a chaotic junk edge sets the remainder
mechanism: Two fields of 8-cell blocks, W = 11010100 left of the head and R = 11110001 right of it. The head is a glider between them: moving right it turns R into W (32 steps per block, GR), moving left W into R (36 steps per block, GL). It bounces between a wall on the left and the tape end, which grows 2 cells per bounce.

Phase S: the wall moves right 18 cells per bounce, leaving an 18-cell wake piece Y (rule S1, exact, 830/830 real bounces). Then one sweep rewrites the wake into 72-cell units V. Phase G: the wall moves back left one unit per 36 bounces while the field gains 18 blocks per unit (rule G36, exact, 86/86 real periods). So the field at the next S start is b' = 9b/4 + c.

The remainder b mod 8 picks the S->G branch (b mod 2 picks the G alignment) and c (-14..+42 seen) comes from the junk left of the wake, which each G->S transition digs into and rewrites: counters inside it are eaten (6,4,3,1,0, then 17,14,12,10,9,7) and the left edge moved from -52 to -111 after 1e10. Halting needs C> 1001; no halt to 4.2e13 (exact accelerated run).

template.diff: 7 transitions (nearest proved table, W4-3c); nothing within 5
template.note: W4-3c (our kill) is a base-3 odometer of flaws in a 0101 stripe; its visit lemmas share nothing with the glider/bounce rules here beyond the picture of defects in a periodic background. Upstream has this table only in Eqv_v2.v TM2413 (an equivalence with our start E), no proof.

strategy: Not a proof yet. Next: an exact cycle accelerator (GR, GL, S1, G36 plus measured S->G branches by b mod 8 and direct runs of G->S) to follow 100+ cycles and census the junk shapes. If they close up (finitely many shapes up to counters), write the branch table and an invariant; otherwise park as a cryptid.
risks: The junk edge is rewritten every cycle by a branch chosen by b mod 8 under b' = 9b/4 + c: pseudo-random input, so the junk shapes may never close up.
Two counters in the junk were eaten down (6 to 0, then 17 to 7); when the second runs out, around 1e14-1e16, the regime may change.
The odd-b G alignment and the S->G and G->S transitions are observed only, not written as rules.

checkpoint_questions.text: Three cycles to 1e8: is the boundary between the vertically striped wake (left) and the flat field rows a slow diagonal moving left (phase G, rows ~95-390) followed by a fast sweep to the right (phase S, rows ~390-465)?
Phase S: four bounces: does each left turn land further right (18 cells per bounce, rule S1)?

Cryptid-like (cryptid protocol): the field grows as b' = 9b/4 + c, b mod 8 picks the branch and the junk sets c, and the junk is rewritten every cycle; no halting branch known, no halt to 4.2e13. Park it, or fund one 2 h stage for an exact cycle accelerator and a census of junk shapes?

status_reason: Mechanism found and the phase rules are exact (GR, GL, S1, G36 validated on random and real instances), but the cycle law b' = 9b/4 + c branches on b mod 8 and on a junk edge that each cycle rewrites; cryptid protocol: rules formalized, flagged, stopped. No halting branch known (halting needs C> 1001).
